introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
incertitudes: Q12(a) : le graphique est a tracer par le candidat ; le corrige donne le tableau des frequences cumulees et la description du trace. La mediane vient de l'interpolation (38,6) ; la lecture graphique attendue est voisine.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The marks obtained by 60 students in an examination were grouped into classes and their corresponding frequencies listed in the distribution table below.

| Marks ($x$) | 0 - 9 | 10 - 19 | 20 - 29 | 30 - 39 | 40 - 49 | 50 - 59 | 60 - 69 | 70 - 79 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No. of students ($f$) | 5 | 7 | 8 | 11 | 13 | 8 | 6 | 2 |

(a) Draw the cumulative frequency graph for the above distribution. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Cumulative frequency table.** The classes are integer marks, so the class boundaries are $-0.5,\ 9.5,\ 19.5,\dots,\ 79.5$. Plot each cumulative frequency against the **upper class boundary**.

| Upper boundary | 9.5 | 19.5 | 29.5 | 39.5 | 49.5 | 59.5 | 69.5 | 79.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 5 | 12 | 20 | 31 | 44 | 52 | 58 | 60 |

Check: the last value equals $5+7+8+11+13+8+6+2=60$ students ✓.

**Graph.** Mark equal scales on both axes (for example $2$ cm for $10$ marks on the horizontal axis and $2$ cm for $10$ students on the vertical axis, from $0$ to $60$). Plot the points $(-0.5,0)$ (start of the curve), $(9.5,5)$, $(19.5,12)$, $(29.5,20)$, $(39.5,31)$, $(49.5,44)$, $(59.5,52)$, $(69.5,58)$, $(79.5,60)$ and join them with a smooth S-shaped curve (an ogive), steepest around $x=40$ to $50$ where the classes are largest.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Hence, estimate the median mark. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $60$ students the median corresponds to the cumulative frequency $\dfrac{60}{2}=30$. On the graph, draw a horizontal line from $30$ on the vertical axis to the curve, then drop a vertical line to the $x$-axis.

Check by interpolation in the class $29.5$ to $39.5$ (cumulative frequency $20$ to $31$):

$$\text{median}\approx29.5+\frac{30-20}{31-20}\times10=29.5+9.09=38.6.$$

**Median mark $\approx38.6$ (about $39$).**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Find the mean of the distribution. *[4 marks]*
(d) Find the variance of the distribution. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the formula $\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum fx^2}{\sum f}-\bar x^2$ with the totals of the table in part (c): $\sum fx^2=105035$, $\sum f=60$, $\bar x=37.5$.

$$\sigma^2=\frac{105035}{60}-37.5^2=1750.58-1406.25=344.33.$$

(Standard deviation $\sigma=\sqrt{344.33}\approx18.6$.)

**Variance $\approx344.3$** (exactly $\dfrac{1033}{3}$).
